subject: Implement composition in the workspace adapter: members and delegated roots, output claims, agreement and export bundle IO, source snapshots, journaled multi-repository federation writes with recovery
description:
WHY: the spec's sections on composition and implementation ownership, contract and release binding (snapshots, release), and changes across repositories, plus the federation rows of agent tools and the workflow-gate rule of engineering order. Acceptance scenarios: interrupted cross-repository write; missing child or wrong digest.

GROUNDING:
- resolveOwner: discover.ts:102-142 (SCOPE_OVERLAP at :119-121); overlapFindings :332-356; a descriptor governs its own root :165-166.
- Tests that keep an undelegated overlap refused: scope.test.ts:25, :70; init.test.ts:44, :56.
- Bundles at `.loom/contracts/<publisher>/<contract>@<version>.json` (published.ts:12, :20-43).
- gatherEvaluationInputs: trust.ts:228-267. pinRevisionSet: :275-300.
- Output collisions are checked against ancestors only (outputs.ts:127-135). InstallJournal and recoverInstall: :224-307.
- `check --all`: packages/cli/src/commands.ts:187-219.

CHANGE:
- Ownership:
  - Registered member roots are delegated and do not overlap; a parent `.` with a child implementation claim stays SCOPE_OVERLAP.
  - A composition-only workspace may have an empty scope.
  - Declared output claims, checked against ancestors, descendants and declared claims.
- Bundles and snapshots: bundles namespaced by member, carrying sourceCommit; source snapshots with contentDigest and inputFiles; a revision vector across members (task 11).
- Federation:
  - inspect returns members, pins, ownership, missing inputs and the dependency graph.
  - plan returns a ChangeProposal (membership, agreement, export-pin or output-ownership changes). Its impact names the frozen components it crosses and the generated artifacts.
  - check takes an optional snapshotDigest and validates a CompositionRelease record as a complete qualified selection. Release assembly stays with workflow integration.
  - apply takes locks in canonical repository order through FederationJournal prepared→applying→complete or recovery-required. Recovery never overwrites an external edit.
  - Integrate task 11's incomplete-journal readiness rule with real journals, and re-verify it here: an interrupted apply blocks composed readiness and release.
  - publish: child exports before parent pins. A release publication requires acceptance or evidence and refuses a snapshot with dirty:true. A draft is never trusted.
  - Never move a gitlink.
- Workflow gate: `check` and `check --all` fail, independently of any agent, on each of:
  - missing required context (a missing member checkout, an unresolved input);
  - stale or empty pins;
  - an incomplete federation journal;
  - an unqualified implementation.
  Each has a failing-check test.
- Tests use real nested git repositories (testing/helpers.ts gitInit): an interrupted write with an external edit during recovery; child-change impact; a missing child and a wrong digest.

AREA TESTS: npm run build; each packages/workspace/dist/test/*.test.js file, one by one; the new composition.test.js; node --test --test-concurrency=1 --test-name-pattern "check" packages/cli/dist/test/cli.test.js; core battery.
WORKER: loom-worker (Sonnet 5, effort high, as its definition sets), resumed across its milestone while its context allows (task 1, warm reuse); Opus at xhigh only through `ledger escalate <task>` when the task proves complex, meaning an unresolved design question or a defect the worker cannot land (owner rule: prefer Sonnet; Opus xhigh only for complex work).
